sync.title: Strategy and Leadership in the Age of AI
sync.rawTitle: #10 - Xavier Ferràs: Strategy and Leadership in the Age of AI | Leading in AI Podcast
sync.youtubeDescription:
Xavier Ferràs is Full Professor at Esade, Associate Dean of the Executive MBA and one of the leading voices on innovation in Spain. He has spoken at more than 200 conferences on strategy, innovation and technology, and his research looks at how AI is redefining competition.

In this episode he explains why we are still in a "fluid phase" of AI, why he thinks companies should slow down, what a Chief AI Officer really needs to know, and why Europe needs a Sputnik moment.

Topics covered:
- Why innovation needs public policy, not only markets
- What the PC, the internet and mobile tell us about AI
- Why the race for bigger models looks unsustainable, and why smaller specialized models may win
- Why companies should not rush: AI is non-deterministic technology
- The Chief AI Officer: strategy, technology and humanism
- Where to start: from conventional processes to new business models
- Europe in the AI race

editorial.summary: Xavier Ferràs is a Full Professor at Esade and Associate Dean of its Executive MBA, and one of Spain's leading voices on innovation, having spoken at more than 200 conferences on strategy, innovation and technology. His research looks at how AI is redefining competition. In this conversation he explains why AI is still in a fluid phase, why the race for ever-bigger models looks unsustainable and smaller specialised models may win, and why companies should not rush a technology that is non-deterministic. He sets out what a Chief AI Officer needs, from strategy and technology to humanism, where organisations should start, and why Europe needs a Sputnik moment in the AI race.
editorial.hook: Why companies should slow down on AI, and why Europe needs a Sputnik moment.
